extracted.intended_audience: software engineering researchers and practitioners interested in code/peer review practices
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical study of contemporary software peer review practices using quantitative measures (e.g., review interval, reviewer count, defect-proxy metrics, and knowledge-sharing). Compares industry projects (Google, Microsoft, AMD) with traditional inspection and open source projects to identify convergent and divergent practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameters of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of measurable characteristics that define peer review practice in contemporary software projects; the paper finds these parameters converge across diverse settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite different settings, cultures, incentive systems, time pressures, etc., the authors observe convergence in the parameters of peer review across projects. Use these parameters as a basis for comparative analysis between projects and against traditional inspection and OSS practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review interval
rubrics_metrics.description: The time span associated with a review (how long reviews take or the latency of the review process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as one of the core measures in the study; can be used to compare responsiveness and turnaround across projects and review regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of developers involved in review
rubrics_metrics.description: The count of distinct developers who participate in reviewing a change or artifact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a measure of social participation and breadth of scrutiny; helpful for assessing review thoroughness, knowledge distribution, and coordination costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proxy measures for defects found during review
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect metrics used to estimate the number or severity of defects discovered during peer review (the paper uses proxy measures rather than direct defect counts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because direct defect labeling may be unavailable, the study employs proxy measures to estimate defects found in review. These proxies should be chosen and interpreted carefully, acknowledging limitations and potential biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of knowledge sharing during review
rubrics_metrics.description: A measure introduced by the authors that quantifies how peer review increases developers' knowledge about the codebase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This dimension captures the informational/learning benefits of review beyond defect detection. The paper introduces a specific metric for knowledge sharing and contrasts it across projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase in distinct files known per developer (knowledge-sharing result)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observed quantitative outcome: conducting peer review increases the number of distinct files a developer knows about by 66% to 150%, depending on the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This concrete result illustrates the magnitude of knowledge diffusion attributable to review in the studied projects and can serve as a benchmark for evaluating review practices' impact on cross-file familiarity.
